subject: Renewal: usage volatility smoothing & term consolidation
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Grant <alex.grant@helionova.com>, Susan Lee <susan.lee@helionova.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 19 May 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: usage volatility smoothing & term consolidation

Alex / Susan —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. We understand HelioNova's usage has been spikier than forecasted as you ramp the new inference pipelines, and you asked for a renewal structure that: (1) locks-in a favorable blended price for the committed baseline, (2) provides a short-term buffer for month-to-month volatility, and (3) consolidates multiple contracts into a single multi-term agreement to reduce admin overhead.

High-level proposed approach (we can iterate):
- Term: 24 months consolidated (current setup is two separate 12-month agreements).
- Baseline commit: 1.2M tokens/month equivalent (annualized), priced at the renewal unit rate.
- Volatility buffer: 125% burst pool applied monthly for first 6 months, billed at a discounted overage rate (50% of list overage).
- True-up cadence: Quarterly true-ups instead of annual to reduce backdated surprises.
- Transitional credit: $120k one-time credit applied to Q1 invoices to offset migration spikes.

Attached I pulled together a short term sheet and an ops checklist for billing and PO timing. If this approach looks sensible, can we schedule a 30-minute sync early next week to finalize numbers and routing?

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Sr. Account Executive, Renewal & Expansion
Redwood Inference
[attachment: Redwood_TermSheet_HelioNova_v3.pdf (PDF, 92KB)]
From: Alex Grant <alex.grant@helionova.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Susan Lee <susan.lee@helionova.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 May 2028 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: usage volatility smoothing & term consolidation

Kimberly —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear options. A few immediate clarifying points from our side:
1) The 1.2M baseline looks reasonable as a committed floor, but we need a smoother ramp month-to-month for the first quarter because the primary customer pilots are unpredictable.
2) Can the burst pool be auto-renewed for months where utilization stays above 110% of baseline? That would reduce manual approvals.
3) On the transitional credit: we need that to be applied as credits that offset invoices rather than a rebate at the end of the quarter. Cashflow is tight with the pilot.

If you can confirm the mechanics for auto-renew and invoice-applied credit we can fast-track. Our procurement lead (Susan) needs to see the final PO-friendly term sheet and the SOW-level billing milestones.

Best,
Alex
Alex Grant
Head of Procurement
HelioNova

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Grant <alex.grant@helionova.com>, Susan Lee <susan.lee@helionova.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 May 2028 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: usage volatility smoothing & term consolidation

Alex —

Thanks for the notes. Quick answers and a small revision we think will make procurement and finance comfortable:

- Auto-renew of burst pool: Yes — for the first 6 months the burst pool will automatically renew each month if utilization >110% of baseline for that prior month. Renewals will be capped at the 125% buffer and won't trigger additional committed baseline increases. Ops will email a monthly summary to your billing contact before any renewal takes effect.

- Credit mechanics: We can apply the $120k as invoice credits split across the first two monthly invoices (60/40) so there is immediate invoice relief. We'll mark the credit lines on the invoice PDF and include a credit memo for your records.

- PO/term sheet changes: I attached a slightly revised term sheet that: (a) adds the auto-renew wording, (b) clarifies credit application as invoice credits, and (c) includes a PO-friendly signature block for Susan.

Proposed next steps:
1) If you and Susan are good with the revised term sheet, I can send the DocuSign link for signatures and loop in legal for a short SLA addendum.
2) David and Marissa will run billing setup and confirm invoice cadence (we'll propose 30-day net, with Q-trues).
3) We target go-live for the consolidated term on June 1 to capture May usage under the new buffer rules.

Can you confirm availability for a 30-minute signature/ops sync on Monday 5/22 at 11:00am PT? If not, propose an alternate.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Sr. Account Executive, Renewal & Expansion
Redwood Inference
[attachment: Redwood_TermSheet_HelioNova_v3.pdf (REVISED) (PDF, 98KB)]
From: Susan Lee <susan.lee@helionova.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Alex Grant <alex.grant@helionova.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: usage volatility smoothing & term consolidation

Kimberly —

Thanks for the quick updates and the revised term sheet. The invoice-credit mechanic and the split (60/40) across the first two invoices looks good for cashflow. The auto-renew behavior for the burst pool is acceptable as described — helpful that it won't auto-increase baseline commits.

I attached the PO and have initial internal approval to sign once DocuSign is received. One small ask from finance: can the invoice memos include the original invoice's usage lines next to the credited lines for ease of reconciliation? If so that's a non-issue.

We can do the 5/22 11:00am PT sync — I'll sign the DocuSign once it hits my inbox.

Appreciate the responsiveness here.

Regards,
Susan Lee
CFO, HelioNova
[attachment: HelioNova_PO_2028.pdf (PDF, 24KB)]
